FYI - the upstream zserge/webview has been detached from boscop/web-view. So that ETA you mentioned is something that we will probably never see in the near future. 

See here:
https://github.com/Boscop/web-view/tree/master/webview-sys

Thanks! Aparently there is an init method for edge webview [here](https://github.com/Boscop/web-view/blob/master/webview-sys/webview_edge.cpp#L303) that runs [here](https://github.com/Boscop/web-view/blob/master/webview-sys/webview_edge.cpp#L287).
If it works, we could use it to run some JS, but I don't know if it is usable yet. Will do some more testing and report any findings here

Edit:
Part of the MSEdge issue seems to be using async script execution, ~~possibly on a new thread~~(probably not, just async with the result not handled). So it can run before the webview is available.*  Source [here](https://github.com/Boscop/web-view/blob/master/webview-sys/webview_edge.cpp#L311), docs [here](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/api/windows.ui.xaml.controls.webview.invokescriptasync)

Edit 2:
We should probably open an issue on webview

*I don't know C++, don't quote me on any of this.
This may have been resolved in webview 0.6.
I will try it later tonight or tomorrow.
I'll redo my tests later tonight, with the latests webview. Will post update here

This should be an issue on webview not tauri. There isn't much that we can do from our side of the fence about this.  

If I had to guess as to whats going on, I would guess that the threading isn't perfect between the webview thread and the rust main thread.  If you run this code multiple times, you will eventually get a program that renders all of the elements.  

![timer](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22513880/72231513-e101ba80-3589-11ea-85bb-35ee70884c20.png)

issue.body:
Issue tauri-apps/tauri#212 is still a problem during windows development,
This is only a problem when `devPath` in `tauri.config.json` is a url, and not a static folder.

Since this is an issue upstream, there is little we can do but wait for the issue to be solved in web-view.

An easy work around is adding the following code in main.js or the equivalent file:
```js
if (!window.tauri) {
  require('../src-tauri/tauri.js') // change this path as needed
}
```
Maybe this should be added to the docs?
